story_description: As a developer, I need the Codex adapter to communicate with the Codex CLI via stdio JSON-RPC so that long-lived sessions work correctly with streaming events and conversation resume.
task_description: On thread/resume, the Codex server returns stored items from the conversation history. Meanwhile, the local streaming buffer may have accumulated newer items during the resume request. CodexItemMerger deduplicates by itemId, keeping the richer version (more content) for each conflict. Handles the edge case where a streaming item arrives after resume completes.
atom: A001-CODEX-ITEM-MERGER Intelligent merge of resume vs streaming items
atom_description: CodexItemMerger provides merge(remote:local:) function that takes remote items from resume response and locally accumulated streaming items, returning a merged array with no duplicates. For each itemId present in both sets, the version with more content wins. Content richness is measured by: (1) presence of non-empty content field, (2) total byte length of serialized item, (3) presence of metadata fields. Handles race condition where streaming item arrives after resume response processing completes by exposing mergeIncremental(existing:newItem:) for single-item updates.
problem_statement: When resuming a Codex session, there is a race condition between the server response and local streaming. The resume RPC returns the canonical conversation history, but streaming events may have already accumulated locally (user sent a prompt, streaming started, then resume response arrives). Without intelligent merging, we either lose the streaming updates (if we replace with remote) or have duplicates (if we concatenate). This atom implements the merge algorithm that every-code uses: compare by itemId, keep the richer version.

notes: This algorithm is critical for resume correctness. The key insight from every-code: streaming can produce items before resume completes, and the local version may actually be richer (has streaming deltas the server has not yet persisted). Default to server authority only when richness is truly equal. The byte count heuristic works because richer items have more content fields populated.
